races.name: Free Tips On attheraces.com Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Jack Sparowe
runners_data.note: In fine recent form — won at Goodwood over 10f in his latest start — and is a natural hold-up horse whose true style is to race well off the pace, though in this field he is pushed into midfield by several other rear-dwellers competing for the same ground; the 61-day absence is worth monitoring but he arrives race-fit.|

runners_data.name: Booziebrunch
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front-runner and will likely lead from stall to straight; trainer S Woods has a modest 14-day strike rate and this three-year-old has won twice over 10f on good, but today's polytrack standard is a slightly different test — the blinkers help her focus and she dictates this race's entire complexion.|

runners_data.name: Eagles Attire
runners_data.note: Unknown quantity with a short, uninspiring form string (three runs, all at 8f or shorter) and over 100 days off the track; the step up to 10f on a surface where she has no prior experience makes her a speculative runner, and Daniel Muscutt will need to find some cover early.|

runners_data.name: Barbury Boy
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on good ground at Goodwood but has only once raced on an artificial surface (11th of 15 at Lingfield in a 7f maiden); the hold-up style means Harry Vigors will need to plot a patient route, and the class step into a handicap with no AW turf experience at this trip is a real concern.|

runners_data.name: Alice De Clare
runners_data.note: Progressive filly who won her last two on good ground over 10f and steps back on to polytrack having placed once from three AW starts; Callum Shepherd has placed horses well this season and a prominent berth from the outset gives her every chance to make her form count.|

runners_data.name: Turku
runners_data.note: Has raced exclusively on AW surfaces in recent runs but without winning — 0 wins from four similar-going starts — and the visor goes on for the first time; Simon & Ed Crisford's yard is in good form over 14 days but Turku's form string has been consistently disappointing on the surface she faces again today.|

runners_data.name: Kaaranah
runners_data.note: Hard to oppose on recent form — four wins from 12 AW starts including three victories at 10f on standard-going — and carrying top weight at 142lbs is the primary concern; Jack Callan rides well at Lingfield and John Butler's yard is firing with a 5/18 14-day record, making this runner the standout on profile.|

runners_data.name: City Of God
runners_data.note: Has won over 8f on standard AW going but steps up in trip to 10f, which is untested on this surface; the tongue-tie goes on and Finley Marsh takes a 5lb claim, which brings the weight down to a workable level — showed he can act on polytrack when winning at 8f, but whether the extra two furlongs suit is the open question.|

runners_data.name: Barry's Boy
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on standard AW and has placed twice more at the same trip; today's 10f is a step up that his pedigree could handle, and George Bass provides able placing skills — the modest trainer 14-day record (0/4) tempers enthusiasm, but he arrives fresh enough after a 38-day break and a hold-up run could suit if the pace is honest.|

races.paceDynamic: Booziebrunch is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival to press her, she is set to control the pace from a prominent position around the outside of the Lingfield polytrack loop, likely bowling along at a measured, sustainable tempo over this 1m2f trip. The trio of Alice De Clare, Kaaranah, and Turku will also be keen to race prominently, meaning the section immediately behind Booziebrunch will be competitive, but none are likely to mount a serious early challenge to her lead. That controlled, even gallop over a flat track typically compresses the finish, rewarding horses who travel fluidly in mid-to-close range rather than deep closers who need a true test — prominently-placed, front-rank profiles are advantaged when the pace is honest but not searching. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can show at the rear: Jack Sparowe is a genuine hold-up horse redistributed to midfield because Barry's Boy, City Of God, and Barbury Boy also profile as rearward runners, and only some of them will secure genuine space behind the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Booziebrunch Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Booziebrunch secures the lead unchallenged and sets a consistent, unhurried tempo that suits front-rank travellers.
scenarios.body: Booziebrunch dictates from flag to flag over the flat polytrack circuit, and the measured gallop means those racing in close proximity — Alice De Clare and Kaaranah — can sustain their effort into the straight without being buried. This shape strongly suits prominently-placed horses with the tactical speed to press the leader at the two-furlong pole.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Front Pair Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Booziebrunch and one of the prominent challengers kick early in the straight, running out of reach of the hold-up brigade.
scenarios.body: With a slow-to-moderate tempo collapsing into a sprint home, the gap to the closers becomes insurmountable and the winner emerges from the front two or three racing throughout. Kaaranah's excellent recent course-and-distance form and Booziebrunch's gate-to-wire profile make them the prime beneficiaries of this scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is faster than expected and the front rank tie up inside the final furlong, handing late movers a window.
scenarios.body: Barry's Boy or Barbury Boy, tracking at the rear of the midfield, could deliver a sustained late run if the principals over-commit from a prominent position. This scenario is discounted because Jack Sparowe — the most natural hold-up horse — is redistributed to midfield and unlikely to produce a true rails-sweeping finish from his natural spot.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Grinder Lands
scenarios.trigger: If the race becomes tactically muddled with multiple prominent horses disputing, creating a moderate but scrappy pace that suits a grinding traveller.
scenarios.body: Congestion early from Alice De Clare, Turku, and Kaaranah could produce pockets and checking through the race, rewarding a horse that finds a clean passage from midfield. Eagles Attire is unproven at this trip and distance combination, but City Of God's course form gives him an outside chance in a messy shape.

watchPoints.text: Kaaranah carries 142lbs at the top of the weights but arrives with a four-from-fifteen AW record including three wins at this exact trip and surface — watch whether the burden blunts her usual late kick.|

Booziebrunch must secure the lead cleanly from her draw; if Alice De Clare or Turku push her into a faster early pace than intended, the front runner could empty inside the final furlong and unravel the dominant scenario.|

Barbury Boy has virtually no AW experience and Harry Vigors (5lb claim) will need to find a clean passage from a hold-up position — watch for the combination getting blocked in the straight on the polytrack's tight bend.|

Eagles Attire is 101 days off the track and races over a trip she has never attempted; Daniel Muscutt's instructions in the early furlongs will be telling — if she travels kindly, the fresh legs could make her interesting in a compressed finish.|

The multiple prominent runners (Alice De Clare, Kaaranah, Turku) bunching behind Booziebrunch could produce significant interference through the first half of the race — watch which of the three gets the best of the early jostle, as that position could prove decisive.|

races.name: Follow @AtTheRaces On X EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Band D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Emilies 21st Birthday Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Quick Quasar
runners_data.note: The only genuine front-runner in the field; won over this exact course-and-distance 13 days ago on Standard going and goes well fresh — the race is his to lose from an uncontested lead, though his OR has risen since that win.

runners_data.name: Midnight's Dream
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse in visor; placed three times in seven recent starts on Standard surfaces but the sheer volume of closers in this field means he is unlikely to get his true rearward position, tempering his effectiveness.

runners_data.name: Wind Summer
runners_data.note: 136-day break is a concern for a 3-year-old; has shown ability to place on Standard going and was second over 7f/8f here, but the layoff and the apprentice booking introduce risk despite sound course form profile.

runners_data.name: Francisco
runners_data.note: Carries a tongue-tie and has won twice from hold-up tactics — but the race shape here, with a controlled pace, is the wrong environment for a true closer; his two wins came on Standard going so the surface is fine, just the scenario that is against him.

runners_data.name: Chelio
runners_data.note: Prominent-racing 3-year-old who has placed at 7f on Standard going and 8f here; 69-day absence is a mild flag but Denis Coakley's horses often return fit, and Chelio's natural front-tracking style is well-suited to sitting just off Quick Quasar.

runners_data.name: Blue Samuna
runners_data.note: Consistent form figures on Standard 7f suggest course aptitude but has yet to win or place in six starts on this surface; the headgear note (hood) may sharpen focus, though Robert Havlin cannot paper over a losing run here.

runners_data.name: Captive Beauty
runners_data.note: Placed in his most recent 7f Standard outing and tracks the pace naturally; Ross Burdon's 3-year-old is lightly raced and the prominent style means he will be positioned to challenge if the winner tires, though the form line is thin.

runners_data.name: My Dad Tom
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon runner who has finished sixth in six of his last seven starts including twice over 7f Standard — his form suggests a deep-midfield type who rarely lands a blow, and the cluttered midfield in this race does him no favours.

runners_data.name: Oxford Circus
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with a poor recent record on Good ground; his one win came on Standard going over a shorter trip, and the prominent style means he could find an inside rail run if the field bunches, though ability to compete at this level is in question.

runners_data.name: Lerwick
runners_data.note: Aged six but fit on a 9-day turnaround; genuine hold-up performer wearing blinkers/cheekpieces, with a win over 8f Good in his last five — probably needs the front group to flatten out to make his late run count on this shorter 7f trip.

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Breeze
runners_data.note: Consistent front-tracking type who has won over 7f Standard and placed twice recently on Good; Gary Moore's stable in decent form (T14: 4/23), Finley Marsh rides, and the prominent style is ideally suited to tracking Quick Quasar through the race.

runners_data.name: Split Elevens
runners_data.note: Outstanding course specialist — two wins and seven places from 13 runs over 7f Standard, jack Callan rides; the 46-day break is the only query on an eight-year-old who clearly loves Lingfield, and he arrives late from genuine hold-up ground.

runners_data.name: Elvetham
runners_data.note: Has won three times over 6f Standard and placed twice more — an AW specialist shifting up to 7f here; the step in trip may not suit his sharp-speed profile, and though he often races prominently the redistribution note confirms he is a true closer pushed forward on this map.

races.paceDynamic: Quick Quasar is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no meaningful challenger for the lead, will dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the gates at Lingfield's 7f. Chelio, Captive Beauty, and Spirit Of Breeze will press forward into prominent positions behind the pacesetter, creating a compact early bunch rather than a true headlong gallop. The field nominally contains several hold-up horses — Midnight's Dream, Francisco, My Dad Tom, and Elvetham — but so many genuine closers are present that the map cannot accommodate all of them at the rear; the prominent berths are most likely to be secured by Chelio, Spirit Of Breeze, and Captive Beauty, with the redistributed hold-up types forced to race in a muddled midfield pack. With one front-runner setting a measured, uncontested tempo over 7f on a Standard AW surface, this race shape strongly favours horses who can track just off the pace and pounce entering the straight — prominent-to-midfield stalkers who cover their ground efficiently without needing a true end-to-end test.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Quasar Controls, Stalkers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Quick Quasar sets a comfortable, uncontested lead and the prominent horses track within striking range throughout.
scenarios.body: Quick Quasar dictates a fair but not punishing pace, and horses like Spirit Of Breeze and Chelio, sitting just off the shoulder, have the energy reserves to challenge off the bend and run through the line; this is the default shape and the AW surface rewards those who travel smoothly in second or third.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Quasar Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so controlled that Quick Quasar conserves enough energy to keep finding and wins from the front.
scenarios.body: With no horse able to pressurise the leader at any stage, Quick Quasar simply slows the race to a crawl and kicks off the home bend, exploiting a winning 7f Standard run on similar going just 13 days ago; the stalkers find the winner has simply stolen too many lengths.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Thread Through
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace proves deceptively strong enough that the front group ties up inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Split Elevens, who has outstanding course form over this exact trip and surface, arrives late with a sustained run; Lerwick, a genuine hold-up performer with a recent win, can also pick up pieces if the field opens a passage, rewarding the few authentic closers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Scrimmage Favours Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If the midfield becomes congested and a lightly-regarded prominent type finds an unexpected run to the inside.
scenarios.body: With so many redistributed hold-up horses clogging the midfield, a runner like Captive Beauty or Oxford Circus finds cleaner air on the rail and benefits from a tactical mess that disrupts the fancied closers; this is a low-probability scenario dependent on significant positional chaos.

watchPoints.text: Quick Quasar's uncontested lead is the defining tactical factor — watch whether any of the prominent types (Chelio, Spirit Of Breeze) elect to press him earlier than expected, which would transform the race from a solo cruise into a genuine test.

Spirit Of Breeze's draw and early positioning will be critical — if he can slot in second or third behind Quick Quasar without burning energy, his proven 7f Standard course form makes him a major threat in the straight.

Split Elevens has an exceptional Lingfield 7f AW record (2W7P from 13 runs on this surface) and Jack Callan knows the track well — monitor whether a clear late passage materialises for this deep closer.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses (Midnight's Dream, Francisco, My Dad Tom, Elvetham) risks creating a congested midfield entering the home straight — any traffic incident there could benefit the front-tracking horses who have already cleared the jam.

Wind Summer's 136-day absence combined with the apprentice booking (Dominique Van Der Kraats, 7lb claim) is a combination to note — if the filly needs the run she will drift back and become a non-factor, but if sharp she rates a place prospect given her 7f Standard placed form.

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Porfin
runners_data.note: Phil McEntee runner returning after 46 days, but boasts 1W5P in similar Standard AW going and the 6f trip is right in her wheelhouse; prominent racing style suits this configuration perfectly and Grace McEntee keeps the booking in-house — most course-proven of the pressing pair.

runners_data.name: Roman Spring
runners_data.note: Fresh off a run just 5 days ago and has barely any AW Standard form (3/15 in similar going), which is a concern on this surface; prominent racer who should sit second or third, but the going record suggests she is better on turf Good ground and connections have a modest T14 strike rate of 0/9.

runners_data.name: Zaltalla
runners_data.note: Gary & Moore operation in solid form (4/23 T14) and David Probert is a quality booking; a natural hold-up horse who is genuinely running from that position — best recent effort was 2nd over 8f Standard, so the step back to 6f and the likely slow pace is not ideal for her finishing style.

runners_data.name: My Mate Mackley
runners_data.note: Adam Kirby-trained 3yo with a tidy place record (0W but consistent), yet his natural hold-up style cannot be accommodated at the back of a field this congested — he will likely race closer than ideal, which dilutes the late-run profile that underpins his form; the 4-day turnaround is quick but he is clearly in good enough nick.

runners_data.name: Real Gold
runners_data.note: Cook & Bridger runner who has placed in four of his last five over 6f AW Standard — the most consistent finisher in the race — but a natural hold-up type who similarly cannot get to the rear given the race shape; 14-day gap is fine and the 6f trip suits, though he has yet to win.

runners_data.name: Ridger
runners_data.note: Tagged as fading in the finish with three poor recent efforts (6,9,9) and a thin AW Standard record (0W0P in 2 similar-going runs); Ollie Sangster has 3 winners from 13 over 14 days but this horse arrives out of form and is the hardest to recommend in the field.

runners_data.name: Pure Passion
runners_data.note: Won over 5f on Good last time (4d ago by race-day) and now steps up to 6f AW Standard where she is the clear pace-setter; Chloe Lyons (7lb claim) helps offset the 137lb weight, trainer Stuart Williams has 3 wins from 32 over 14 days — gets a dream lead if rivals let her dictate.

runners_data.name: Dr Ali
runners_data.note: Jenkins runner with the best overall AW Standard win record in the field (2W5P in 13 similar-going runs), but placed in the midfield on the map because the surplus of hold-up types forces him forward from his natural position — the hg:v headgear is noted and the 5-day turnaround is brisk; if he can somehow find the back of the field this is a live each-way candidate, but it is structurally unlikely.

runners_data.name: Global Effort
runners_data.note: Returning after a long 150-day break, which is the most significant fitness query in the race; a natural hold-up horse who, like Dr Ali, is mapped to midfield due to congestion at the rear, and his recent 5f AW form has been uniformly poor (finishing 6th-9th repeatedly) — the step back from a lengthy absence makes him the hardest to trust.

races.paceDynamic: Pure Passion is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the early lead, she will dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from stall to the Lingfield AW bend at roughly the 4f pole. Porfin and Roman Spring will track closely in the prominent positions, ensuring at least some coverage of the leader without applying serious pressure, meaning the pace is unlikely to be truly searching. The hold-up brigade — Zaltalla, Real Gold, Dr Ali, My Mate Mackley, and Global Effort — will be grouped in the pack, but with so many natural hold-up types chasing limited real estate at the rear, several will find themselves racing closer to the pace than their preferred style demands; Dr Ali, My Mate Mackley, and Global Effort are redistributed to midfield on the map precisely because none can realistically reach the back of the field in this configuration. A controlled single-file gallop on a flat AW circuit at 6f strongly favours the horse that leads or sits closest to the pace and quickens from a position of comfort — the prominent/pressing profile is best placed to exploit what is essentially an uncontested lead.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pure Passion Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Pure Passion is allowed to dictate a measured pace with no rival pressuring her for the lead, she converts her recent winning form into a wire-to-wire success.
scenarios.body: Racing fresh off an 8-day back win, Pure Passion has the highest OR in the field and will enjoy a supremely comfortable life on the front end with Chloe Lyons (7) able to control fractions; hitting the straight first and with daylight to aim at, she is hardest to pass on a flat circuit.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Reel Her In
scenarios.trigger: If Pure Passion sets a fractionally stronger early tempo and ties herself up in the final furlong, the pressing pair behind capitalize.
scenarios.body: Porfin — with solid 6f AW Standard course form (1W5P in similar going) — and Roman Spring, sitting a length or two off the pace, are ideally positioned to collar a weakening leader in the final 100 yards; both carry the profile of horses who travel well in the box seat and pick up once daylight appears.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string out the field and the front end fades badly in the final furlong, a hold-up type gets home.
scenarios.body: Zaltalla (best OR-adjusted recent form in the hold-up group, 2nd at 8f Standard) is best qualified to finish off a truly run race, though Real Gold's consistent place record at 6f AW Standard keeps her relevant; this scenario is discounted because the redistribution of Dr Ali, My Mate Mackley, and Global Effort means the true hold-up horses are not actually running from far back.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — No Clear Winner
scenarios.trigger: If early jostling disrupts the pace map entirely, with multiple horses disputing the lead and the race becoming ragged, an each-way outsider exploits the confusion.
scenarios.body: A scrambled early order could see Roman Spring or even My Mate Mackley (sharp enough over 5f, quick out of stalls) get involved up front and unsettle Pure Passion's rhythm; the beneficiary in this messy shape is most likely whichever prominent horse finds the cleanest passage through the melee.

watchPoints.text: Pure Passion's early gallop is the race — if she is allowed to coast in front unchallenged, she is very hard to catch on a flat 6f AW circuit; watch whether Porfin or Roman Spring apply any pressure before the 3f pole.

My Mate Mackley, Dr Ali, and Global Effort are all natural hold-up horses who cannot get to the rear of this field — watch whether they end up racing two to three lengths closer than their usual position, which will affect whether any late challenge materialises.

Global Effort returns from 150 days off and is the only runner with a fitness concern of that magnitude; watch the market in the final hour and how he moves in the paddock, as a big layoff over AW on unfavourable form makes him high-risk.

Ridger's three consecutive tail-end finishes (6th, 9th, 9th) and the fade-in-finish flag make him a race-map passenger rather than a contender — watch whether he has any early foot or simply slots in at the rear throughout.

Roman Spring's AW Standard record is thin (3 similar-going runs, 1W2P all on turf Good) — watch whether she travels as smoothly as her turf form suggests once the kickback hits on the Lingfield polytrack.

races.name: Become A Friend Of Racing Welfare Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Neswick
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced Marcus Tregoning filly with only one run to her name (third over 1m2f on this surface), whose running style is unclassified — but the step up to this trip on familiar going is a logical fit, and David Probert's booking gives her a fair chance of settling into a handy position.|

runners_data.name: Oklahoma Dream
runners_data.note: David Menuisier's filly is a natural hold-up horse who wears a hood, with two outings both resulting in fifth; this race's likely steady pace is a concern for her profile as she needs horses to come back to her rather than having to make her own progress.|

runners_data.name: Paraone
runners_data.note: Completely unexposed on debut for Heather Main with going and style data both unknown — Finley Marsh rides and the absence of any public trial form makes her the biggest question mark in the field, capable of anything from an eye-catching run to anonymity.|

runners_data.name: Protectrix
runners_data.note: John Butler's filly was beaten in seventh on her sole start over 7f on this surface, so the step up to 1m2f looks like an improvement opportunity, but her style is unclassified and the trainer's current form (5/18 over 14 days) suggests the yard is ticking over without excelling.|

runners_data.name: Shangri La
runners_data.note: David Simcock's hold-up filly has shown mid-table consistency in form (443-5) over varying trips and surfaces; her true racing style is at the rear of the field, but the congestion of closers in this race means she may find herself racing further forward than ideal — a factor that could compromise her chance if the pace is weak.|

runners_data.name: Walking On Stars
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's filly is the race's lone confirmed front-runner and will dictate the tempo uncontested; her two runs have resulted in a fifth and a fourth, both on this surface and trip, but the ability to control proceedings from the front is a major tactical asset in this field even with a modest form profile.|

runners_data.name: Blue Hill
runners_data.note: Ismail Mohammed's prominent-type is the most likely horse to track Walking On Stars throughout and represents an each-way danger if the Prescott filly fades late; she has two placed efforts over 1m1f and 1m on AW, suggesting this trip extension is worth a chance.|

runners_data.name: Champagne Beau
runners_data.note: Patrick Chamings' hold-up filly carries a "fades in finish" flag, having finished eighth and ninth in her two starts on Good and Soft ground — this steady AW gallop does nothing to help her, and the going switch to Standard is unproven for her.|

runners_data.name: Dove Tale
runners_data.note: The Gosden-trained filly has the most relevant course-and-distance form in the field (third over 1m3f on this surface) and is a natural hold-up type, so while the likely steady pace is not ideal, her AW experience and powerful stable connection make her a credible threat in any scenario where pace materialises.|

races.paceDynamic: Walking On Stars is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no credible challenger for the lead, Sir Mark Prescott's filly will dictate tempo from the front at a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 1m2f Lingfield AW trip. Blue Hill is the only other natural prominent-type and may track Walking On Stars in second, but neither horse has the profile to inject serious early pressure, meaning the early sectionals will almost certainly be modest. Shangri La is a genuine hold-up horse redistributed to the midfield in the map because this field contains more hold-up types than can all realistically race at the rear — Oklahoma Dream, Champagne Beau, and Dove Tale are all natural closers competing for the same late-race ground. A steady, uncontested gallop set by Walking On Stars will compress the field, reduce the advantage of pure hold-up horses, and favour a prominent or handy tracking profile that can strike from a good position turning for home — the prominent-to-midfield profile is the one best-placed to capitalise on this race shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Tracks
scenarios.trigger: If Walking On Stars bowls along unchallenged and sets a measured, even tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: Walking On Stars dictates from the front at a pace that suits her, with Blue Hill tucked in behind and able to strike turning for home; the steady gallop means the closers never get a true stamina-test to reel back the leaders.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closer Gets Home
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely honest enough that a late-running profile can close off a strong final furlong.
scenarios.body: Despite the lone front-runner profile, if Walking On Stars goes quick enough early — or if Blue Hill pushes the tempo — one of the true closers can pick them off late; Dove Tale's recent third over course and distance makes her the most credible beneficiary of this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Poaches Race
scenarios.trigger: If Walking On Stars is allowed to stride clear early and the field dawdles while the closers are stuck behind each other.
scenarios.body: With no pressure whatsoever and a field of novices who may not appreciate the danger until it is too late, Walking On Stars steals enough of a cushion that the hold-up horses simply cannot make it up; Prescott's record of exploiting this exact scenario adds weight to the risk.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Scrimmage, Upset
scenarios.trigger: If the race develops chaotically with hold-up horses shuffled wide or blocked, causing a muddled finish.
scenarios.body: A bunched novice field with several unproven types could produce a messy finish where an unknown quantity like Paraone or Neswick, racing with minimal pressure on their rating, emerges from the chaos; this remains a low-probability but live threat given the number of lightly-raced horses.

watchPoints.text: Walking On Stars (front-runner) risks slipping the field if the hold-up horses are slow to spot the danger — watch her early sectionals for any sign of a Prescott-style front-running theft.

Shangri La is a genuine hold-up horse who may be forced to race in midfield due to the density of closers in this field — watch for her being caught in traffic turning for home rather than finding clear daylight.

Champagne Beau has a documented pattern of fading in the finish and arrives here having never run on an AW surface — watch for whether she travels with any enthusiasm before the straight or drops away tamely.

Dove Tale runs just 8 days after her last start, a short turnaround for the Gosden yard on a horse still finding her feet — watch her in the paddock for any signs of residual freshness or fatigue before the race.
Paraone is a debutante for Heather Main with no trial data — watch for market moves in the final 30 minutes before post time as a guide to how connections rate her chance behind closed doors.

races.name: Download The At The Races App Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Wolf's Gallop
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer for Tom Lacey — four runs all at 5f with a string of placed efforts on good ground, suggesting this AW standard surface is untested but the distance is proven; Charles Bishop takes over and 15 days between runs is a freshness positive at this mark.

runners_data.name: Beautiful Effort
runners_data.note: Ismail Mohammed and Jose Santos yard have gone 0/7 in the past 14 days, and this filly's best effort came on AW standard going (a narrow third), but 6f form dominates her record so the step back to 5f is a query; 36 days off and a wider draw could see her swept aside in the early rush.

runners_data.name: Sultan Darius
runners_data.note: Marco Botti sends Darragh Keenan aboard a horse who has run three times without breaking 4th, all over 5-6f on good ground — the switch to AW standard is unexplored and his prominent style will put him in the firing line of the pace duel; 2/15 trainer strike rate over 14 days is modest.

runners_data.name: Stoney Wood
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse that fades in the finish — a significant structural concern on a flat 5f where there is nowhere to hide — and all three AW starts have returned placed or beaten efforts with no win; Callum Shepherd takes the ride but the pattern here is of a horse running out of stamina rather than finishing through.

runners_data.name: Miss Moneypit
runners_data.note: Rod Millman's filly has won over 5f on good and has a genuine prominent racing profile, but the field density means she is unlikely to secure that position today — she drops back from a 12-day turnaround with David Probert booked, and her best chance depends on getting a clear run from a midfield berth she would not naturally choose.

runners_data.name: From Me To You
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's hold-up filly has a blinker flag and a 0/4 record on similar AW standard going — the one AW start returned a 6th at 6f — and her 23-length beaten run at 5f on good is an alarming data point; Joe Leavy faces a stern task getting her competitive from the back.

runners_data.name: Secret Rival
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's confirmed front-runner has gone 0/3 in her career with best effort 6th at 6f on good — no form to suggest she can sustain the lead when South West presses her hard; George Downing takes the ride and 28 days between runs is straightforward enough, but her raw figures are light.

runners_data.name: South West
runners_data.note: The highest-rated runner in the field at OR 75 with a win over this exact 5f trip on good ground, and Richard Hughes's stable has fired in 3/30 over 14 days — blinkers applied and Finley Marsh maintains the partnership; the key question is whether he can settle in front after a contested early break rather than burning his petrol in a duel with Secret Rival.

runners_data.name: American Psycho
runners_data.note: Archie Watson's hold-up runner is the classiest closer in the field by RPR (134) with a second at 5f on good ground and an AW start already on his record; 1/29 trainer strike rate over 14 days tempers enthusiasm, but his profile is structurally suited to picking up the pieces if the pace war takes its toll.

runners_data.name: Viking Barbie
runners_data.note: Ollie Sangster's prominent filly brings the most consistent placed form in the race — 4-2-3-4 across her last four at 5-6f on good — and Daniel Muscutt is a strong AW jockey booking; 41 days between runs is the longest gap in the field and is worth monitoring, but her draw and tactical awareness could see her slot comfortably into a prominent berth behind South West.

races.paceDynamic: South West and Secret Rival are confirmed front-runners and will battle for the lead from the off on this flat Lingfield AW 5f, creating a genuinely contested gallop rather than a dawdle. Wolf's Gallop, Sultan Darius, Viking Barbie, and Beautiful Effort all want prominent positions, generating a congested early order that will compress the field and heighten traffic risk between the 2f and 3f pole. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race can accommodate — South West, with the highest OR and a proven win over the course and distance, is best placed to secure the lead, with Viking Barbie and Wolf's Gallop most likely to claim the prominent slots ahead of Miss Moneypit, who is a genuine prominent racer but will be pushed wider and further back than ideal. An honest, pressured pace on standard AW ground favours runners who can sit just off the speed and sustain their effort through the final furlong — the prominent-off-pace and late-midfield profiles are structurally advantaged here over true hold-up horses who will face a wall of horses in front.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Duel, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If South West and Secret Rival fight hard for the lead, burning each other off and handing the race to a close-tracking prominent runner who saves ground.
scenarios.body: The sustained early pace bleeds the two leaders in the straight, and a horse that has tracked just behind them — saving vital energy through the middle section — produces a strong, sustained finish to the line. Wolf's Gallop and Viking Barbie, both consistent front-rank types with speed figures to match this standard, are ideally positioned to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If South West leads without serious interference after the first furlong and settles into a controlled rhythm that his rivals cannot disrupt.
scenarios.body: South West has the highest OR in the field, a proven win at 5f on good ground, and a jockey booking that suggests confidence — if the pace dynamic settles quickly and he dictates on his own terms, he is hard to pass on this track. His blinkers application and Richard Hughes training form in the past 14 days add further substance to this reading.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pack collectively goes too fast early and the hold-up horses find clear daylight down the outside entering the final furlong.
scenarios.body: American Psycho, with an RPR of 134 and a second at 5f on good ground, is the most credible closer in the field and needs the pace to collapse in front of him. From Me To You and Stoney Wood have hold-up profiles but lack the form figures to inspire strong confidence, limiting this scenario's ceiling.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos, Scrambled Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion between the 2f and 3f poles causes interference, checked runs, and a messy mid-race that scrambles the result.
scenarios.body: With four horses chasing two positions, riders will be competing for every inch of running room approaching the turn into the straight, and any checks or bumps could produce a result that defies the form book. Stoney Wood's noted tendency to fade in the finish makes her an unlikely beneficiary even in chaos, while American Psycho's hold-up position keeps him cleaner.

watchPoints.text: South West and Secret Rival are on a collision course for the lead — watch for an aggressive, sustained duel in the first furlong that could compromise both their chances and set the race up for those tracking behind.

The prominent cluster of Wolf's Gallop, Sultan Darius, Viking Barbie, and Miss Moneypit will create serious crowding between the 2f and 3f marks — runners on the inner are at real risk of being checked or short of room.

Miss Moneypit is a natural front-rank type squeezed into a midfield role by the field's pace density — watch whether David Probert pushes forward early to claim a position, which could further inflame the early pace.

American Psycho is the form pick from the hold-up group but needs the pace to collapse and a clean run down the outside — any traffic on the wide draw will delay his challenge and may cost him vital lengths on this flat 5f.

Stoney Wood has a flagged tendency to fade in the finish — if she is prominent early due to race flow, watch for her to drop out sharply inside the final furlong, potentially causing interference for runners coming through behind her.
